newsitem.title: USA: Smith's Food bonds up 4 pts on acquisition.
newsitem.headline: Smith's Food bonds up 4 pts on acquisition.

text.p: Bonds of Smith's Food & Drug Centers Inc gained four points after news on Monday that general merchandise retailer Fred Meyer Inc would buy the supermarket chain, high-yield traders said.
"Smith's Food 11-1/4 percent bonds rose four points on the positive news," said one trader.
The bonds, due 2007, were quoted 116-3/8 bid, 116-5/8 offered, traders said.

Portland, Oregon-based Fred Meyer, which sells food, jewelry, clothing and other items, said it had signed a definiitive agreement to acquire Smith's Food in a stock swap valued at about $720 million.
Meyer said it will assume about $1.3 billion of Smith's Food debt.
Fred Meyer chief administrative officer Ken Thrasher, said in a conference call with investors on Monday that the company will have $1.5 billion in total debt after the acquisition.
Smith's Food's senior secured debt is rated Ba3 by Moody's Investors Service Inc and holds a senior implied rating of B-plus from Standard & Poor's.
The merger will give the combined company 265 stores in 11 states.
Fred Meyer stock traded off 1/8 at 41-3/4, while Smith's Food stock gained 3-1/8 to 43-1/8.
